name: Mo'o
description: Shapeshifting lizard spirits in Hawaiian mythology who serve as powerful ancestral guardians (ʻaumākua) of freshwater sources, manifesting as monstrous reptiles, tiny geckos, or humans, and revered as sacred protectors of the land and water.

aliases.name: Moʻo
aliases.meaning: Lizard; also used for succession or continuity — the name carries multiple layered meanings

regions: Oʻahu — particularly Kawainui Marsh (windward) and Waialua
Hawaii Island — various streams and pools
origin: All major Hawaiian islands. Moʻo are associated with specific named water bodies throughout the archipelago. Comparable water guardian traditions exist across Polynesia.
